diagnosis_power.name: Power problem
diagnosis_power.default_recommendation: Check the power connections and try a different wall socket.

diagnosis_display.name: Display problem
diagnosis_display.default_recommendation: Check the monitor cable and try a different port or screen.

diagnosis_boot.name: Boot / operating-system problem
diagnosis_boot.default_recommendation: Try Safe Mode and use the operating system startup repair.

diagnosis_performance.name: Performance problem
diagnosis_performance.default_recommendation: Close background programs and free up disk space.

diagnosis_overheating.name: Overheating problem
diagnosis_overheating.default_recommendation: Check that the cooling vents are not blocked and the fans work.

diagnosis_network.name: Network problem
diagnosis_network.default_recommendation: Restart the router/modem and check the internet connection.

diagnosis_storage.name: Storage problem
diagnosis_storage.default_recommendation: Free up disk space and run a disk-check tool.

diagnosis_memory.name: Memory problem
diagnosis_memory.default_recommendation: Close unused programs and consider adding more RAM.

diagnosis_peripheral.name: Peripheral/device problem
diagnosis_peripheral.default_recommendation: Reconnect the device and check its driver.

intermediate_facts.power_delivery_issue: Possible problem delivering power to the computer
intermediate_facts.internal_power_fault: Possible internal power fault (e.g., power supply)
intermediate_facts.os_boot_reached: Operating system reached the boot stage
intermediate_facts.startup_overload: Too many programs start with the system

rules.explanation: The power cable is not connected firmly, so electricity may not reach the computer.
The wall socket is not supplying power correctly, so the computer cannot receive electricity.
The power LED is off and the system inferred a problem delivering power to the computer, which points to a power problem.
rules.recommendation: Check the power cable connections and try another wall socket. For a laptop, also check the charger.

rules.explanation: Power reaches the computer (cable and socket are fine) but pressing the power button produces no LED and no fans, suggesting an internal power fault such as a failing power supply.
The system inferred an internal power fault because the machine receives power from the wall but cannot switch on. This is a power problem.
rules.recommendation: Check that the power supply connections are seated correctly. If the problem persists, the power supply may need professional repair.

rules.explanation: The computer is running but the screen stays blank even during startup, so no display signal is reaching the screen.
The system first inferred a display-path failure: the computer runs but shows no picture at all. This is a display problem.
rules.recommendation: Check the monitor cable and try a different port or monitor. For a laptop, connect an external screen to test.

rules.explanation: The built-in screen is blank but an external monitor shows a picture, so the laptop still produces a display signal and the screen or its backlight is faulty.
The system inferred that the built-in screen or its backlight is faulty because an external monitor works. This is a display problem.
rules.recommendation: Use an external monitor meanwhile; the built-in screen or backlight may need service.

rules.explanation: The operating system loading screen appeared, so the OS reached the boot stage.
The system inferred that the operating system reached the boot stage, but it then shows an error screen. This indicates a boot or operating-system problem.
rules.recommendation: Try Safe Mode and use the operating system startup repair. If you recently installed software, consider removing it.

rules.explanation: The BIOS screen appears but the operating system never starts loading, so the OS fails to reach the boot stage.
The system inferred that the operating system fails to boot after the BIOS screen. This is a boot or operating-system problem.
rules.recommendation: Try Safe Mode, use a repair/recovery drive, or reinstall the operating system after backing up your data.

rules.explanation: The operating system starts slowly and programs are slow to open, so the system generally runs slowly.
The system runs slowly and the disk is almost full, which explains the poor performance.
rules.recommendation: Free up disk space by removing unnecessary files and programs.

rules.explanation: Many programs start with Windows while the system is slow, so startup is overloaded.
The system inferred a startup overload: too many programs start with Windows, slowing the boot and responsiveness.
rules.recommendation: Disable unnecessary startup programs from Task Manager.

rules.explanation: The computer is running and hot, but the cooling fans are not spinning, so cooling is not working.
The computer is hot and its ventilation openings are blocked, so heat cannot escape.
The system first inferred a cooling problem, which combined with unexpected shutdowns supports an overheating diagnosis.
rules.recommendation: Check that the cooling vents are not blocked and verify that the cooling fans are operating normally.

rules.explanation: The computer is unusually hot, its fan is loud, and it shuts down unexpectedly — classic signs of overheating.
rules.recommendation: Clean the dust from the fans and vents and make sure nothing blocks the airflow.

rules.explanation: The computer is connected to Wi-Fi and reaches the router, but cannot reach the internet, so connectivity works only locally.
The system inferred that connectivity works only inside the local network. Since the internet is unreachable, this is a network problem.
rules.recommendation: Restart the router and modem. If the problem persists, contact your internet service provider.

rules.explanation: No Wi-Fi networks are visible and other devices are offline too, so the network itself is failing.
rules.recommendation: Restart the router. If it still fails, check the internet connection with your service provider.

rules.explanation: The computer is connected to Wi-Fi and can reach the router, but it does not obtain a valid IP address, indicating a network problem.
rules.recommendation: Renew the IP address (release/renew in the network settings) and restart the router.

rules.explanation: The disk is almost full and constantly busy, so it is under storage pressure.
The system inferred storage pressure because the disk is nearly full and continuously active, indicating a storage problem.
rules.recommendation: Free up disk space by removing unnecessary files, emptying the recycle bin, and uninstalling unused programs.

rules.explanation: The disk reports errors and files are missing or corrupted, which indicates a storage problem.
rules.recommendation: Back up your important data and run the operating system's disk-check tool to look for bad sectors.

rules.explanation: RAM usage is near its limit and the system freezes, so memory is under pressure.
The system inferred memory pressure because RAM is nearly exhausted and the system freezes, indicating a memory problem.
rules.recommendation: Close unnecessary programs and consider adding more RAM.

rules.explanation: Some installed RAM is not detected and applications crash frequently, indicating a memory problem.
rules.recommendation: Reseat the memory modules and test each memory stick individually.

rules.explanation: The device is not detected in any port and also fails on another computer, so the device itself is faulty.
rules.recommendation: Try the device on another computer to confirm. If it fails there too, the device may need replacement.

rules.explanation: The device is not detected in the original port but works in a different port, so the original port is faulty.
rules.recommendation: Use the working port or have the faulty port checked.

rules.explanation: The device is detected but the operating system shows a driver problem, so the device cannot be used correctly.
rules.recommendation: Reinstall or update the device driver from Device Manager.
